source.title: EvoLM: In Search of Lost Training Dynamics for Language Model Reasoning
source.authors: Zhenting Qi; Fan Nie; Alexandre Alahi; James Zou; Himabindu Lakkaraju; Yi-Lun Du; E. Xing; S. Kakade; Hanlin Zhang

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream performance across pretraining-token budgets and model sizes, and relates validation perplexity to downstream accuracy, but does not fit or test the original held-out-loss scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper uses the Chinchilla ratio to guide its pretraining budgets but does not test a compute-optimal loss allocation. Its own scaling results measure benchmark accuracy, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy. Rows below capture downstream scaling and validation-PPL correlations relevant to V6, plus upstream accuracy trends that do not fit a listed version. The paper's discussion of scaling laws and results cited from other studies are not recorded as its own results.
record.test_reason: The study trains its own 0.5B/1B/4B models over 10–320B-token budgets and reports benchmark and post-trained reasoning accuracy by tokens and size. This bears on V6 in a new setting: post-trained generative reasoning. It fits no scaling law and measures no held-out pretraining loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors find diminishing returns from excessive pre-training and post-training, with possible OOD degradation. Model size pays off only once pretraining reaches the saturation regime; under limited budgets, smaller models can match or beat larger ones. They also find ORM scores predict downstream accuracy better than validation loss. They make no claim about loss power laws.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains 0.5B, 1B, and 4B models over token-budget sweeps and evaluates benchmark accuracy and post-training outcomes; it does not fit held-out-loss power laws or estimate compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Downstream outcomes vary with pretraining-token budget and model size; OOD metrics can decline after overtraining.

fits_no_version.finding: For post-trained variants of one 1B base, validation perplexity barely correlates with downstream Maj@16 accuracy (r² 0.000–0.219), while ORM score correlates strongly (0.62–0.84).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: After post-training, validation loss stops tracking downstream reasoning accuracy across post-training configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: Scaling SFT and RL data or epochs improves ID accuracy with diminishing returns. OOD accuracy peaks and then declines (SFT epochs 2–4), and Pass@16 degrades with excess RL.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream returns to post-training compute saturate, and can reverse out of domain.

fits_no_version.finding: Intermediate checkpoints at 20/40BT from a 160BT run underperform fully decayed runs of the same length, upstream and on MATH (Table 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Using intermediate checkpoints in place of fully scheduled runs biases scale comparisons.

record.problems: The study evaluates models only up to 4B parameters and reports benchmark accuracy rather than held-out pretraining cross-entropy. Several downstream trends are described from figures without numerical values in the text. The validation-PPL comparison is on post-trained variants and does not establish prediction from pretraining loss.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible result rows left out.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss is measured or fitted.
No fit on small runs and no extrapolation.
No loss-minimising allocation is estimated. The Chinchilla ratio is only used to set budgets.
No shape variants at fixed parameter count.
Fine-tuning and RL scaling report accuracy only, with no power-law fit of loss.
No predictive fit or extrapolation of downstream accuracy. No link from pretraining loss to downstream accuracy.
No fitted exponents or compared fits.

missing.what: Table 4 per-size, per-token benchmark averages (1B: 46.44, 49.38, 51.88, 52.30, 52.49 at 20–320BT; 4B: 50.22, 55.30, 56.94 at 80–320BT). R21/R22 could carry these values.
Equal-token comparison at 80BT: 1B vs 4B ID Maj@16 14.1/21.4 vs 13.2/20.0 (SFT/SFT+RL), and OOD Maj@16 24.6/31.0 vs 23.4/29.6. The larger model is not better.
OOD and Pass@16 columns of Table 1 at 160BT (e.g. OOD Maj@16 25.6/31.6 vs 26.0/33.2), showing the size gain extends to OOD.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3: the setting is post-trained reasoning, and no loss-scaling method is used. Models go only up to 4B, the analysis is qualitative, and there are no fits. Several trend claims rest on figures without transcribed values.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss scaling is measured.
No power-law fit on small runs or extrapolation to larger runs is reported.
No loss-minimising parameter/token allocation is estimated at fixed compute.
The paper does not compare architecture variants at fixed parameter count.
Only language-model training is studied; other modalities and the listed alternative regimes are not tested.

The study assesses downstream accuracy across pretraining-token budgets and model sizes, and validation PPL across post-trained variants. It does not test downstream prediction from held-out pretraining loss or fit a general predictive scaling law.
No fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits are compared across setups or fitting choices.

relationships.condition: Model size at 160BT pretraining tokens (1B vs 4B, post-trained), and benchmark accuracy rising with tokens and size in the low-budget range
relationships.reason: 4B beats 1B at 160BT (ID Maj@16 26.4 vs 14.2 SFT; 34.8 vs 22.5 SFT+RL; R10–R13). 1B SFT ID Maj@16 rises 8%→15% from 20 to 80BT (R1). Benchmark accuracy rises with tokens (R21, R22).
relationships.display_finding: At 160BT, 4B exceeded 1B on ID Maj@16 after SFT (26.4 versus 14.2) and SFT+RL (34.8 versus 22.5), while increasing pretraining from 20 to 80BT raised 1B SFT ID Maj@16 from 8% to 15%, with benchmark accuracy also rising with tokens.

relationships.condition: Pretraining tokens beyond ~80BT for 1B models; equal-token comparison at 80BT
relationships.reason: Gains saturate after 80BT: ID Maj@16 goes 15%→17% at 320BT, RL shows negligible benefit, and benchmark accuracy gains less than 1 point (R1, R5, R21, R22). At 80BT the 4B model does not beat the 1B (Table 1, from the text; no row yet).
relationships.display_finding: Beyond 80B tokens, ID Maj@16 rose only from 15% to 17% at 320B, reinforcement learning added negligible benefit, and benchmark gains stayed below one point; at 80B tokens, the 4B model did not outperform 1B.

relationships.reason: The authors state that OOD Maj@16, RM@16 and Pass@16 decrease after 160BT; values are figure-only (R2–R4).
relationships.display_finding: Out-of-distribution Maj@16, RM@16 and Pass@16 decreased as pretraining increased from 160BT to 320BT.
